messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: multiple serving-runtime OOMs + node flaps detected in eu-west. Pager triaged to on-call. severity=P2

incident-bot: summary=CUDA OOMs, container crashloops, autoscaler rapid scale events. first seen 03:08 UTC. alert: https://alerts.internal/2776549876

raj: ack, i'm primary. grabbing kube events, hpa history and recent deploys.

sara: seeing 40+ scale events in 10m from hpa(rapid up/down). pods entering CrashLoopBackOff with exit 137 and occasional device resets.

alex: adding metrics: gpu_mem_used spikes at startup, concurrent allocs > available on warmups. client errors: 502/503 briefly. CS pinged.

raj: kube events excerpt:

```
Nov 03 03:08:12 kubelet[1234]: Node node-09 NotReady: network plugin timed out
Nov 03 03:08:13 kubelet[1234]: Pod serving-runtime-xyz terminated with exitCode=137 (OOM)
Nov 03 03:08:15 cloud-autoscaler: scale from 2 -> 8
Nov 03 03:08:22 cloud-autoscaler: scale from 8 -> 3
Nov 03 03:08:30 kernel: NVRM: GPU at 0000:af:00: Device has been lost
```

raj: hypothesis: new runtime image + no autoscaler cooldown caused mass concurrent warmups; GPUs hit peak allocations and driver resets -> pods crash -> autoscaler interprets as insufficient capacity and flips more nodes -> thrash.

sara: @deploy-bot any recent runtime rollout?

deploy-bot: runtime-image:v3.8.1 rolled out 02:55 UTC -> 100% by 03:05. No kernel/driver package changed in the image.

nora: taking ops note: will pause autoscale, set hpa min replicas to current stable (4), disable scale-to-zero, and add 2m stabilization-window.

alex: please also block new deploys to runtime-image until we confirm.

nora: executing: `kubectl patch hpa serving -p '{"spec": {"minReplicas": 4, "maxReplicas": 4}}'` and `kubectl annotate hpa serving autoscaler.k8s.io/suspended=true`

raj: cordon node-09 and node-10, drain if necessary. prefer graceful but will delete stuck pods to avoid long warmups.

```
kubectl cordon node-09
kubectl drain node-09 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --timeout=5m
```

raj: while draining, found preStop hooks blocking; deleted a few pods to speed recovery. post-delete, new pods start but hit OOM on first allocation.

sara: applying mitigation: route 40% traffic to cached smaller model (redwood-slim) for eu-west, reduce max concurrent tokens to lower per-request memory.

alex: triggered runtime rollback to v3.7.9 as canary (2 pods) at 03:24 UTC.

deploy-bot: rollback initiated -> runtime-image:v3.7.9 canary 2/2.

nora: monitoring driver logs during canary: canary shows stable GPU memory footprint on start, no device lost messages.

raj: after 18 minutes of canary, error rate dropped from 6.8% -> 0.9%, p95 latency back to baseline. autoscaler still suspended.

cs-bot: Customer Impact: degraded generation service for eu-west between 03:08-03:40 UTC. Affected orgs: 5, active sessions impacted approx 150. CS notifications sent.

alex: handoff: raj you lead post-incident analysis, sara on autoscaler tuning, nora on deploy gating. I'll coordinate customer comms with CS.

raj: immediate followups created:
- add 120s cooldown and stabilization-window to GPU-backed HPA, increase target memory buffer to 20%
- add rollout throttle for GPU runtime images (max 20% per 10m)
- implement warmup prefetch for model KV to avoid big concurrent allocations during scale-ups
- add alert for rapid HPA flapping (>=5 scale events in 5m) to detect thrash earlier

sara: PR opened for autoscaler changes: https://git.internal/pr/12678 (include tests).

nora: created ticket to add deploy-gate that disallows full rollout unless canary telemetry shows stable mem profile for 15m. https://issues.internal/8890

alex: posted external status: "We experienced degraded performance in EU region due to a runtime warmup issue. Mitigations in place; full service restored. Followup postmortem planned."

raj: incident mitigated at 03:40 UTC. leaving runbook and logs at https://runbooks.internal/incidents/2776549876. scheduling postmortem.

incident-bot: INCIDENT 2776549876 status -> MITIGATED at 03:40 UTC. Postmortem created: https://postmortems.internal/2776549876

cs-bot: follow-ups scheduled; CS sent individualized notes to impacted customers.

alex: thanks team. we'll reconvene for postmortem review tomorrow.
